name: Leon Gao
life: “I learned engraving by cutting each of my sisters' names into cheap teaspoons.” Monday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Leon stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I've made two tags with different sounds. You can tell who's coming down the stairs without looking.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a red windbreaker and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Leon has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, with brown hair pinned away from the temples. Leon leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations during a conversation.
personality: Leon can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Leon can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To fit two tags the household can identify by sound alone.
family: Anna Avila is Leon’s second cousin. Leon puts the kettle on. Anna chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *A widow bids again*, Anna says, “I want ownership shared because the widow's next wife might feel differently about us.”
connections: Adriana Arnett. The delivery picture lets the engraver finish the two distinct tags.
